skill.name: security-patterns
skill.description: Security review guidance for OWASP risks, authentication, authorization, secrets handling, cryptography, headers, and dependency checks.
skill.summary: Review common web security risks using OWASP-focused patterns and local audit helpers.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported many high-risk tokens, but nearly all are educational examples labeled unsafe or grep patterns used by local audit scripts. I confirmed only the executable Bash helper capabilities and local filesystem scanning behavior; I found no hidden exfiltration, prompt injection, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Shell audit helpers execute local commands in the user project.
remediation.suggestion: Document every command the scripts may run and require explicit user approval before Bash execution.

remediation.issue: security-scan.sh can print source lines that match secret patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Redact matched values by default or print only file paths and line numbers unless verbose mode is requested.

remediation.issue: dependency-audit.sh may call package audit tools that contact external services.
remediation.suggestion: Document possible network access and provide guidance for offline or no-network environments.

content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss common web risks and unsafe defaults. This skill gives OWASP-focused checklists, examples, and local audit helpers for faster review.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes OWASP Top 10 risks with prevention guidance.
Provides examples for input validation, output encoding, authentication, and authorization.
Documents password hashing, session cookies, JWT, OAuth, MFA, and rate limiting patterns.
Explains cryptography choices for hashing, encryption, signatures, random values, and key storage.
Lists HTTP security headers and framework-specific implementation examples.
Includes shell scripts for local grep-based checks and dependency audit commands.
limitations: It is guidance and pattern matching, not a complete penetration test.
Several examples intentionally show unsafe code for comparison.
The audit scripts require local tools such as rg, git, npm, or language scanners.
Results need human review to separate real issues from false positives.

use_cases.title: Review a web feature before release
use_cases.description: Use OWASP checklists to inspect access control, validation, sessions, headers, and logging before deployment.

use_cases.title: Create secure implementation guidance
use_cases.description: Turn authentication, cryptography, and header patterns into practical review notes for a project team.

use_cases.title: Run quick local security checks
use_cases.description: Use the included scripts to find common risky patterns and dependency audit gaps in a repository.

prompt_templates.title: Check common risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature for common OWASP risks. Focus on input validation, output encoding, authentication, authorization, and secrets handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review authentication flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of login and sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authentication flow. Check password hashing, session cookies, reset tokens, MFA, rate limits, and account lockout behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Assess cryptography choices
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of sensitive data handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these cryptography choices. Verify algorithms, key storage, random value generation, nonce handling, signatures, and password hashing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a release security audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pre-release review across a repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release security audit plan for this repository. Include manual checks, local script checks, dependency review, and follow-up fixes.

output_examples.input: Review a login endpoint and session configuration.
output: Findings grouped by authentication, session cookies, rate limiting, reset tokens, and logging.
A severity rating for each issue with clear remediation steps.
A checklist of tests to confirm the fixes.

output_examples.input: Assess security headers for a web application.
output: A header-by-header review of CSP, HSTS, framing, content type, referrer, and permissions policy.
Recommended production settings with notes about compatibility tradeoffs.
A short validation plan using browser tools or trusted header scanners.
A workflow that selects the right scanner for Python, Node.js, Go, Rust, and Docker projects.
A review process for advisories, patched versions, and temporary mitigations.
A summary format for release blockers and accepted risks.

best_practices: Treat unsafe examples as teaching material and copy only the corrected patterns.
Run included scripts in trusted repositories and review results before changing code.
Pair automated pattern checks with manual review of business logic and authorization paths.
anti_patterns: Do not treat grep results as confirmed vulnerabilities without context.
Do not copy examples marked wrong into production code.
Do not use the skill as a substitute for threat modeling or expert review.

faq.question: Is this skill for security testing or secure coding?
faq.answer: It supports both, but it focuses on defensive review, secure implementation patterns, and common audit checks.

faq.question: Does it execute scans automatically?
faq.answer: No. It includes scripts that a user may run manually in a local repository.

faq.question: Are the unsafe examples vulnerabilities in the skill?
faq.answer: They are educational examples labeled as wrong or risky. Users should copy only the corrected patterns.

faq.question: Can it find every security issue?
faq.answer: No. Pattern checks miss business logic flaws, design issues, and context-specific authorization problems.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review the included Bash scripts, required local tools, and any audit output before applying changes.
